subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Concept model B: respectful borrowing versus appropriation
task_label: Theatre and movement — Second concept model
essential_question: How can understanding dance, culture, and artistic context help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Build a clear mental model of respectful borrowing versus appropriation through an explicit worked example, demonstration, text, or phenomenon.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of respectful borrowing versus appropriation.
Check, revise, or improve work about respectful borrowing versus appropriation using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about respectful borrowing versus appropriation.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: Day 5 of "Dance, Culture, and Artistic Context" (unit 5, grade 7) is a second concept model on respectful borrowing versus appropriation. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Create or analyze a movement work with context, attribution, and accessible alternatives. Today's work contributes to that by handling respectful borrowing versus appropriation at the concept model b stage, against the unit's wider topics of movement motifs, space time and energy, choreographic structure, and cultural context. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Study a second, contrasting model work for respectful borrowing versus appropriation and set it beside the first one you examined earlier in this unit. Build a comparison naming one choice the two makers share and one place they clearly diverge, with the effect of each difference described in terms a listener or viewer could verify. Then make one short study of your own that borrows the second maker's approach to respectful borrowing versus appropriation. Cite both works. Anything you did not make yourself must be public domain, openly licensed, or properly attributed. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about respectful borrowing versus appropriation, and it belongs to "Dance, Culture, and Artistic Context", which also covers separate topics such as movement motifs. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about respectful borrowing versus appropriation; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about respectful borrowing versus appropriation., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Build a clear mental model of respectful borrowing versus appropriation through an explicit worked example, demonstration, text, or phenomenon.
Produce the deliverable for a second concept model: Two-work comparison naming a shared choice and a divergence, one short study in the second approach, and citations for both works.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Two-work comparison naming a shared choice and a divergence, one short study in the second approach, and citations for both works.
critique_criteria: One shared choice and one clear divergence between the two model works are both named.
The effect of each difference is described in verifiable terms rather than as preference.
A short original study borrows the second work's approach.
Both works are cited; nothing uncredited and nothing outside public-domain or licensed use appears.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting respectful borrowing versus appropriation.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for respectful borrowing versus appropriation follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for respectful borrowing versus appropriation, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for respectful borrowing versus appropriation works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of respectful borrowing versus appropriation, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking respectful borrowing versus appropriation mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply respectful borrowing versus appropriation under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on respectful borrowing versus appropriation rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
